newsitem.title: CANADA: Saskatchewan says SW floods may be record-setting.
newsitem.headline: Saskatchewan says SW floods may be record-setting.

text.p: Saskatchewan spring flood levels in the southwest part of the province are at the second highest level of the century and may soon reach or exceed the top level of the century, Saskatchewan Water Corporation said.

"We are already at the second highest flood level this century and we could equal or better the peak flows for the century," Saskatchewan Water Corp's director of basin operations Alex Banga told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"That's by later this week and in Gravelbourg by tomorrow," Banga added.

Southwest Saskatchewan produced more than 80 percent of Saskatchewan's durum wheat in the 1995/96 (Aug/July) crop year and Saskatchewan overall produced about two-thirds of the durum exported by the Canadian Wheat Board, the CWB has said.
The usually-arid southwest also produces a significant proportion of export quality milling wheat and barley.
"This whole area received 200 percent of normal fall precipitation last fall, coupled with 200 percent of normal snow pack," Banga said.

"Plus the fact that, because of the Chinook winds that come in from the west (Rocky Mountain Range), it's not uncommon for this basin to lose its snowpack almost completely once or twice a winter. It had never lost it once this year," Banga added.
The Notukeu Creek at Vanguard, which has more than 20,000 tonnes of elevator storage capacity at CP Rail System's line southeast of Swift Current, crested Tuesday morning, he said.
"Vanguard probably should be ok," Banga said. "Flows are rising very quickly right now and probably expected to peak in the next 24 to 36 hours passed Gravelbourg on the Wood River."
